clue.text: The way to stimulate progress of a swimmer

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way or road
to urge on is to spur someone forward

explanation.surface: Advice on how to coax a slow swimmer along faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' looks like a person in the pool, but it is a big fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This large fish, the source of caviar, spends its life swimming in rivers and seas.

clue.text: Early snack?

parts.note: read 'Early' as Earl-y, belonging to an earl: the bread-wrapped meal named after the Earl who reputedly ate it at the gaming table

explanation.definitionFit: The Fourth Earl of this title gave his name to filling between bread slices, so the snack is literally an earl's.

clue.text: Pint guest mishandled — doing this to it?

definitions.text: Pint guest mishandled — doing this to it?

indicators.note: letters handled badly get jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy pub guest fumbles a pint, and the question asks what they are doing to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mishandled' rearranges PINT GUEST; the whole clue then describes a guest knocking over a pint, which is what the word means.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking over a glass is tipping it so the beer spills.

clue.text: Drag up honoured companion from the ravine

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' says the word is written bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: to lug is to drag or haul
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone hauls an honoured friend up out of a deep ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LUG into GUL. CH is the Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulch is a narrow steep-sided valley, an American word for a ravine.

clue.text: One endless old drinking-bout is hard to bear

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for the drinking-bout is dropped

parts.note: a rouse is an archaic word for a carousal or bout of drinking

explanation.surface: A single long drinking session leaves someone with a burden hard to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the final E from ROUSE, leaving ROUS. ROUSE is Shakespearean for a drinking bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Something onerous is burdensome, a heavy load to carry.

clue.text: Nick Weaver is one of those up with the drinkers

definitions.meaning: Nick ... is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

definitions.text: one of those up with the drinkers
definitions.meaning: drinkers toast with '... up', so this is one of those raised ...

explanation.surface: A man called Nick Weaver turns out to be a regular among the pub crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick Weaver' reads like a person's name; it is Nick Bottom, Shakespeare's weaver. 'Bottoms up!' is a British drinking toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comic weaver is Nick Bottom, and drinkers raise glasses crying 'bottoms up'.

clue.text: Ape has most of the fruit — a nut perhaps

indicators.note: most of says the word for the fruit loses its last letter

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters of a nut could come out in another order

explanation.surface: An ape eats most of a piece of fruit, and possibly a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the E of ORANGE to give ORANG; 'perhaps' rearranges A NUT into UTAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This red-haired great ape lives in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Having the stomach for an excursion east

parts.note: a trip is an outing or excursion
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone has the nerve, or the stomach, for a journey eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having the stomach' suggests courage; here the stomach itself is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is the stomach lining of cattle, eaten as offal.

clue.text: Very little time

definitions.meaning: tiny, read with the stress on the second syllable
sixty seconds, a unit of time

explanation.definitionFit: The word means tiny when stressed on its second syllable and sixty seconds when stressed on its first.

clue.text: She joins George the writer and artist

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A woman links up with George, the writer, and an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' looks like a man's name but gives SAND, the pen name of a woman novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra is a girl's name, and 'she' stands for any woman.

clue.text: Air supply needed to make this organ function

definitions.text: Air supply needed to make this organ function

parts.words: Air supply needed to make this organ function
parts.note: sounds like a church organ needing air from bellows, but the organ is the nose, breathing in air

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the nose, the organ through which air is breathed in.

clue.text: Oriental isle gets into a mess with this issue

parts.note: E for east, the orient
the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

indicators.note: a mess here is a jumble, so the words into a are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eastern island gets itself into trouble with this matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' rearranges INTO A into ATION. The Isle of Man is a British crown dependency.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that flows or issues out from a source.

clue.text: Turnip! the rallying cry?

definitions.meaning: turnip is old slang for a large pocket watch, so the cry 'Turnip!' is a word for a watch
a slogan or password that rallies a group

explanation.surface: Someone shouting 'Turnip!' as their battle cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnip' was old British slang for a bulky pocket watch, so the vegetable's name is a word for a watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan or motto that unites a group is its watchword.

clue.text: Whence Roland, bearing good news

parts.note: Roland is the horse in Browning's poem How They Brought the Good News from this city to Aix

explanation.definitionFit: In Robert Browning's poem the horse Roland carries the good news from this Flemish city to Aix.

clue.text: Armour of copper is clothing an Abyssinian prince

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: clothing means the word is wraps around the prince, as clothes wrap a body

parts.note: taken as written
Ras is a title of an Ethiopian prince or chief

explanation.surface: A suit of copper armour is worn by an Ethiopian prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Abyssinia is the old name for Ethiopia, where Ras was a princely title.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuirass is a breastplate and backplate, body armour.

clue.text: Raphael, the affable one — it might be the port

definitions.meaning: Milton calls Raphael 'the affable' one of God's chief angels in Paradise Lost
a Russian port on the White Sea

explanation.surface: Raphael, a friendly figure, might turn out to be a seaport.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton's Paradise Lost calls Raphael 'the affable archangel'; the port is in northern Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael is one of the chief angels in scripture, and the same name belongs to a White Sea harbour.

clue.text: Here to witness an international sporting encounter

parts.note: at means in this place, as in 'at home'
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: Come here to watch an international match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket match, played over several days.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness that something is true.

clue.text: Easily nauseated by poor production of his masque

indicators.note: a poor production of a play scrambles it, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatregoer feels sick at a bad staging of someone's masque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor production of' rearranges HIS MASQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeamish person is quickly made queasy or sickened.

clue.text: For ever enthralled apparently, showing devout respect

indicators.note: apparently says the word is plainly visible in the clue words in front

explanation.surface: Someone seems forever enthralled, showing deep devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across fo-REVER ENT-hralled.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverent person shows deep respect, as in worship.

clue.text: Put, say, Maltese award up on the breakfast table

parts.note: eg, for example
Malta was awarded the George Cross, GC, in 1942
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to place Malta's medal on the breakfast table.
explanation.walkthrough: Malta was given the George Cross, GC, for its wartime resistance. 'Put' only links the wordplay to what sits on the breakfast table.
explanation.definitionFit: This small holder for a boiled egg is a fixture of the breakfast setting.

clue.text: Father locks up a social outcast

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' reads the word for locks from bottom to top

parts.note: locks are hair

explanation.surface: A father imprisons a man shunned by society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks up' looks like imprisoning, but 'up' turns HAIR backwards to RIAH.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is someone rejected by society.

clue.text: Look over the 'circuit-breaker ' muddle

parts.note: to con is to study or pore over
a fuse breaks an electrical circuit when overloaded

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the circuit-breaker and gets in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: CON as 'study' is an old literary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To confuse is to jumble up or bewilder.

clue.text: "Now sleeps the _____ petal, now the white" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: "Now sleeps the _____ petal, now the white" (Tennyson)

parts.words: "Now sleeps the _____ petal, now the white" (Tennyson)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Tennyson's lyric in The Princess; the missing word is a deep red

explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's line reads 'Now sleeps the [deep red] petal, now the white', the missing colour opposed to white.

clue.text: One of two measures called by Mark Twain

definitions.text: One of two measures called by Mark Twain

parts.words: One of two measures called by Mark Twain
parts.note: 'mark twain' was the Mississippi leadsman's call for a depth of two six-foot units, and the author took it as his pen name

explanation.definitionFit: A depth of two six-foot units was called 'mark twain' on riverboats, so each is one of those measures.

clue.text: Awful rot written in articles, but it comes from the heart

indicators.note: written in means put inside the two articles

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, twice

indicators.note: awful rot is jumbled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dreadful nonsense in the newspapers, yet sincerely meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' looks like part of the surface's grumble, but it is the anagram signal; 'written in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This main artery carries blood out from the left ventricle.

clue.text: Ring the canon

definitions.meaning: a song in which voices enter in turn with the same melody

explanation.definitionFit: A circle is round in shape, and a canon like 'Frère Jacques' is sung as a round.

clue.text: Put back in office, control political community

parts.note: to rein is to control or restrain
a state is a nation or political body

explanation.surface: Restore someone to office and take control of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone to a former position.

clue.text: Supernaturally acute

definitions.meaning: in music, a note above natural pitch, raised a semitone

explanation.definitionFit: A note raised above its natural pitch is called this, and a keen mind or blade is also so described.

clue.text: This time-keeper's wasted, we hear

parts.note: the timer narrows in the middle, so it is 'waisted', which sounds like 'wasted'

explanation.definitionFit: This sand timer has a narrow waist, giving its name to a figure shape.

clue.text: Quick as a pedestrian who emerges thus from the traffic

definitions.meaning: quick is an old word for living, as in 'the quick and the dead'

definitions.text: as a pedestrian who emerges thus from the traffic
definitions.meaning: someone crossing a busy road who comes out unharmed and breathing

explanation.surface: A pedestrian darts quickly across the road and survives the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' looks like speed but means living, as in the Bible's 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Living and breathing, as in the old sense of 'quick'.

clue.text: Learned cleric enters race at this half way point

indicators.note: enters says the cleric goes inside the race

parts.note: the mile is a running race
DD is a Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A scholarly priest joins a race at the halfway mark.
explanation.walkthrough: A Doctor of Divinity is a cleric with a learned degree; the mile is a classic athletics race.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre is the point halfway between two ends.

clue.text: Picture biscuits taken straight, from the oven

parts.note: ginger snaps are crisp biscuits
food fresh from the oven is hot

explanation.surface: A photo of biscuits fresh out of the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' only links; it fits the photo picture nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph.
